newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota eyes bond issue for new hockey arena.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota eyes bond issue for new hockey arena.

text.p: Minnesota state and local officials have proposed to build a new $130 million arena with public and private financing in downtown St. Paul to attract a National Hockey League expansion franchise.

St. Paul officials had planned to issue $51 million of debt to renovate their existing arena, but an NHL expansion committee found the Civic Center unsuitable during a visit in early April, said Paul Adelmann, spokesman for St. Paul Mayor Norm Coleman.
Under the new proposal, St. Paul would contribute $30 million to a new arena, the expansion ownership group $35 million and the state $65 million, Adelmann said late Monday.
The new facility could be located on the Civic Center site or just to the west of it, Adelmann added.
St. Paul is one of six cities considered finalists for the next round of NHL expansion. The league has not set a date for that expansion or decided how many franchises, if any, it will award.

St. Paul officials had also hoped to lure the former Hartford Whalers to St. Paul when the team decided to leave Connecticut. The Whalers ownership has narrowed its choices to either Columbus, Ohio, or Raleigh, N.C., however, and plans to announce a new home for the franchise by May 10.
"The NHL likes the hockey market and the ownership group, but it is also clear they didn't like the Civic Center," Adelmann said.
St. Paul's $30 million contribution does not include demolition of the existing arena or other infrastructure improvements, city finance director Martha Larson said Tuesday.

The city has not decided what type of debt to issue for the city portion, Larson added. St. Paul has issued its maximum annual general obligation debt allowance of $17.5 million for the current year, she noted.
To issue more general obligation debt this year, the city would need legislative approval or a successful referendum, Larson said.
City officials are looking at an existing $1 per ticket surcharge as a major revenue stream as well as other sources, she said.
Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson has pledged to issue up to $65 million of bonds for a new arena, spokesman Brian Dietz said. Carlson does not want that figure to grow beyond that, however, Dietz said.
Carlson had also supported issuing $51 million of debt for renovating the Civic Center as well as up to $5.5 million upfront this year, Dietz added.
Minnesota operates on a biennium budgeting process and is not currently in a bonding year.
